lines.text: You Didn't Know Banks Don't Keep Everyone's Deposits in Cash.
What if I told you that your bank might not have enough cash to give everyone their money back at once?
But here's how it actually works.
Imagine 100 people each deposit $1,000 into the same bank.
You might think the bank keeps all that cash locked inside a giant vault.
Banks use money to provide loans, make investments, and run their operations.
They keep enough liquid funds to handle everyday withdrawals.
But imagine all 100 customers suddenly demand their money back at the exact same time!
The bank might not have enough cash immediately available.
This is how a bank run can happen.
And it's why banks are regulated and many countries have deposit insurance systems.
So next time you check your bank balance, remember…
Your money isn't necessarily sitting in a vault waiting for you.
It's part of a much bigger financial system.
You didn't know that about money.
